title.zh: 卷141 志一百十六 兵十二 马政
title.raw: 卷141 志一百十六 兵十二 马政

sentences.zh: 志一百十六

translations.literal: Treatise one hundred sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 116

sentences.zh: 兵十二

translations.literal: Military twelve.
translations.idiomatic: Military 12

sentences.zh: 馬政

translations.literal: Horse administration.
translations.idiomatic: Horse Administration

sentences.zh: 清初沿明制，設御馬監，康熙間，改為上駟院，掌御馬，以備上乘。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qing they followed the Ming system and established the Imperial Horse Directorate; during the Kangxi reign it was changed to the Superior Stud, which managed imperial horses to prepare for mounting the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qing dynasty the court followed Ming practice and set up the Imperial Horse Directorate; under Kangxi it became the Superior Stud, charged with imperial mounts for the emperor's riding.

sentences.zh: 畜以備御者，曰內馬；

translations.literal: Horses raised to prepare for imperial riding were called inner horses;
translations.idiomatic: Horses kept for the emperor's use were termed inner horses;

sentences.zh: 供儀仗者，曰仗馬。

translations.literal: those supplied for ceremonial guard were called ceremonial horses.
translations.idiomatic: those assigned to ceremonial escort were called ceremonial horses.

sentences.zh: 御馬選入，以印烙之。

translations.literal: When imperial horses were selected and brought in, they were marked with a branded seal.
translations.idiomatic: Horses chosen for imperial service were admitted and branded with an official seal.

sentences.zh: 設蒙古馬醫官療馬病。

translations.literal: Mongol horse doctors were appointed to treat equine ailments.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol veterinary officers were appointed to treat sick horses.

sentences.zh: 上巡幸及行圍，扈從官弁，各給官馬。

translations.literal: When the sovereign toured or went on hunting expeditions, attendant officials and officers each received government horses.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial tours and hunting expeditions, every attendant official and officer received a government mount.

sentences.zh: 以副都統或侍衛為放馬大臣，主其事。

translations.literal: A vice president of the banner or an imperial bodyguard served as horse-distribution minister and directed the matter.
translations.idiomatic: A banner vice president or imperial bodyguard was named horse-distribution minister to oversee the arrangements.

sentences.zh: 上謁祖陵，需馬二萬三千餘匹，東西陵需馬四千三百餘匹，悉取察哈爾牧廠馬應之。

translations.literal: When the sovereign paid respects at the ancestral tombs, more than twenty-three thousand horses were required; for the eastern and western imperial mausoleums more than four thousand three hundred horses were needed—all supplied from Chakhar pasture horses.
translations.idiomatic: A visit to the ancestral tombs required more than 23,000 horses; the eastern and western imperial mausoleums needed more than 4,300—all drawn from Chakhar stud pastures.

sentences.zh: 迨乾隆時，每扈從用馬匹輒二萬餘。

translations.literal: By the Qianlong era, each imperial entourage routinely used more than twenty thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: By the Qianlong reign, each imperial entourage routinely consumed more than 20,000 horses.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶中，物力漸耗，停木蘭秋獮。

translations.literal: During the Jiaqing period material resources gradually dwindled, and the autumn hunts at Mulan were suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiaqing, resources ran thin and the autumn hunts at Mulan were discontinued.

sentences.zh: 十二年，減額馬之半。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the quota of horses was cut by half.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of his reign the allotted horse quota was halved.

sentences.zh: 道光九年，如盛京謁陵，額馬視乾隆時，約略相等，計取給廠馬暨各盟長所進，蓋二萬六千餘匹雲。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Daoguang, for paying respects at the tombs in Mukden, the allotted horses were roughly equal to those in the Qianlong era; counting pasture horses and contributions from various league chiefs, the total came to more than twenty-six thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 9 (1829), a Mukden tomb visit required a horse allotment roughly matching Qianlong levels; pasture stock plus gifts from league chiefs totaled more than 26,000.

sentences.zh: 順治十五年定軍馬，親王出征，馬四百匹，郡王三百，貝勒二百，貝子百五十，鎮國公百匹，輔國公八十，不入八分鎮國公七十，輔國公六十五，將軍八十，副將軍七十，護軍統領、前鋒統領、副都統皆六十，其下各有差，最少者護軍、領催各六匹。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Shunzhi military horse quotas were fixed: a prince on campaign four hundred horses, a commandery prince three hundred, a beile two hundred, a beise one hundred fifty, a duke of the imperial clan one hundred, a second-rank duke eighty, a duke not in the eight privileges seventy, a second-rank duke sixty-five, a general eighty, a lieutenant general seventy, a guards commander, vanguard commander, and vice president of the banner each sixty, with graded reductions below, the minimum being six horses each for guards and squad leaders.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi 15 (1658) fixed campaign horse allotments: princes 400, commandery princes 300, beile 200, beise 150, imperial dukes 100, second-rank dukes 80, and so on down the ranks to six horses each for guards and squad leaders.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十五年，敕出徵兵一人馬四匹，四人為伍，一伍主從騎八匹，馱器糧用具亦八匹。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Kangxi an edict fixed that each soldier on campaign had four horses; four men formed a squad; one squad had eight riding horses for master and followers, and eight pack horses for equipment, grain, and utensils.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 35 (1696) ordered four horses per campaign soldier; four men formed a squad with eight riding mounts and eight pack animals for gear and provisions.

sentences.zh: 是歲，征噶爾丹，以兵丁馬瘦，褫兵部尚書索諾和職。

translations.literal: That year, in the campaign against Galdan, because the troops' horses were thin, the minister of war Suo Nuohe was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: That year, during the Galdan campaign, emaciated troop horses cost War Minister Suo Nuohe his post.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，覈定軍中職官馬數，大學士、尚書、左都御史十六匹，侍郎以下遞減，經略、大將軍各二十五匹，副將軍以下遞減。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year the horse quotas for military officeholders were verified: grand secretaries, ministers, and the censor-in-chief sixteen horses each, vice ministers and below in descending grades, grand coordinators and commanders-in-chief twenty-five each, lieutenant generals and below in descending grades.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 51 (1712) official horse quotas were audited: grand secretaries and ministers received sixteen each, with graded reductions below; grand coordinators and commanders-in-chief received twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十六年，八旗牧官馬二萬七千七百餘匹，以萬匹於都城外牧養，熱河千匹，各庄頭二千匹，餘者分畀直隸標營。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Qianlong the Eight Banners pastured twenty-seven thousand seven hundred-odd government horses; ten thousand were kept outside the capital, one thousand at Rehe, two thousand at various estate heads, and the remainder distributed to Zhili banner garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong 16 (1751) the Eight Banners pastured 27,700-odd government horses: 10,000 outside the capital, 1,000 at Rehe, 2,000 with estate managers, and the rest assigned to Zhili garrisons.

sentences.zh: 圈馬之設，始乾隆二十八年，從都統舒赫德請也。

translations.literal: The establishment of corral horses began in the twenty-eighth year of Qianlong, following the request of the banner commander Shuhede.
translations.idiomatic: Corral-horse herds date from Qianlong 28 (1763), at the request of banner commander Shuhede.

sentences.zh: 滿洲八旗，旗養馬二百匹。

translations.literal: For the Manchu Eight Banners, each banner pastured two hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: Each Manchu banner pastured 200 corral horses.

sentences.zh: 蒙古八旗，旗百匹。

translations.literal: For the Mongol Eight Banners, each banner one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Each Mongol banner pastured 100.

sentences.zh: 洎五十九年撤圈，分給各兵拴養。

translations.literal: By the fifty-ninth year the corrals were abolished and the horses distributed for individual soldiers to tether and raise.
translations.idiomatic: By Qianlong 59 (1794) the corrals were dissolved and horses issued for soldiers to keep individually.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十二年，諭成親王永星議復圈馬，大學士戴衢亨等會議，立章程十條，圈馬仍舊。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Jiaqing the emperor ordered Prince Cheng Yongxing to discuss restoring corral horses; Grand Secretary Dai Yuheng and others met in conference, established ten articles of regulation, and corral horses were restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaqing 12 (1807) the throne ordered Prince Cheng Yongxing to study restoring corral herds; Grand Secretary Dai Yuheng's conference produced ten regulations and reinstated the old system.

sentences.zh: 道光末，軍興遂廢，後亦不復籌矣。

translations.literal: At the end of Daoguang, with warfare arising, it was abandoned, and afterward was never revived.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Daoguang, war ended the practice for good and it was never revived.

sentences.zh: 同治元年諭曰：「馬政廢弛，積弊已深，以致軍馬罷瘠。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi an edict stated: "Horse administration has fallen into neglect; long-standing abuses run deep, so that military horses are exhausted and emaciated.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhi 1 (1862) brought an edict: "Horse administration has decayed; abuses run so deep that army mounts are spent and thin.

sentences.zh: 牧廠大臣等應妥實整頓，差功罪以挽頹風，著為令。」

translations.literal: Pasture ministers and the like should thoroughly rectify matters, distinguishing merit and fault to reverse the declining trend, and this is to be established as regulation."
translations.idiomatic: Pasture officials must set things right, rewarding merit and punishing fault to reverse the decline—let this stand as permanent law."

sentences.zh: 溯自世祖入關，迄於康、乾之際，盛京、吉林、黑龍江、直隸、江南、浙江、廣東、福建、湖北、四川、陝、甘、山東、山西諸省設駐防滿洲營，馬凡十萬六千四百餘匹，惟福建水師駐防僅數十匹。

translations.literal: Tracing from when the founding emperor entered the Pass down to the Kangxi and Qianlong era, garrison Manchu camps were established in Mukden, Jilin, Heilongjiang, Zhili, Jiangnan, Zhejiang, Guangdong, Fujian, Hubei, Sichuan, Shaanxi-Gansu, Shandong, and Shanxi, with horses totaling one hundred six thousand four hundred-odd; only the Fujian naval garrison had several tens.
translations.idiomatic: From the Shunzhi conquest through the Kangxi and Qianlong heights, Manchu garrisons across fifteen provinces mustered 106,400-odd horses—Fujian's naval garrison alone held only a few dozen.

sentences.zh: 乾隆季年，定西藏兵制，前藏供差營馬六十匹，後藏二十匹，舊塘四十三，共塘馬二百二十匹，新設番塘二十四，共番馬九十八匹。

translations.literal: In the late Qianlong years Tibet's military establishment was fixed: front Tibet duty horses sixty, rear Tibet twenty, old courier stations forty-three totaling two hundred twenty station horses, newly established Tibetan stations twenty-four totaling ninety-eight Tibetan horses.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Qianlong, Tibet's military horse quotas were set: 60 for front Tibet, 20 for rear Tibet, 220 for 43 old courier stations, and 98 for 24 new Tibetan stations.

sentences.zh: 黑龍江兵向無額馬，道光十六年，從哈豐阿請，始設置之。

translations.literal: Heilongjiang troops had never had allotted horses; in the sixteenth year of Daoguang, following Hafeng'a's request, they were first established.
translations.idiomatic: Heilongjiang troops had no allotted horses until Daoguang 16 (1836), when Hafeng'a's memorial led to their establishment.

sentences.zh: 天聰時，征服察哈爾，其地宜牧，馬蕃息。

translations.literal: In the Tiancong era Chakhar was conquered; the land was suitable for pasture and horses multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tiancong (1627–1636), the conquest of Chakhar opened excellent pastureland where herds multiplied.

sentences.zh: 順治初，大庫口外設種馬廠，隸兵部。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi a breeding-horse pasture was established outside Daku Pass, subordinate to the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: Early Shunzhi saw a breeding stud founded beyond Daku Pass under the Board of War.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年，改牧廠屬太僕寺，分左翼右翼二廠，均在口外。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi pasture administration was transferred to the Court of the Imperial Stud, divided into left-wing and right-wing pastures, both beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 9 (1670) placed pastures under the Court of the Imperial Stud as separate left- and right-wing herds beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 是時，大凌河設牧廠一，邊牆設廠二，曰商都達布遜諾爾，曰達里岡愛，隸上駟院。

translations.literal: At that time one pasture was established at Daling River and two along the border wall, called Shangdu Dabusun Nur and Daligangai, subordinate to the Superior Stud.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Daling River gained one pasture and the border wall two—Shangdu Dabusun Nur and Daligangai—under the Superior Stud.

sentences.zh: 尋分設牧廠五，曰大凌河牧群馬營，曰養息牧哈達牧群馬營，曰養息所邊外蘇魯克牧牛羊群，及黑牛群牧營，曰養息牧邊外牧群牛營，並在盛京境。

translations.literal: Soon five pastures were separately established: the Daling River horse herd camp, the Yangxi Mu Hada horse herd camp, the Yangxi Office border Suluk cattle and sheep herd and black cattle herd camp, and the Yangxi Mu border cattle herd camp—all within Mukden territory.
translations.idiomatic: Five more pastures followed in Mukden territory: Daling River horse camp, Yangxi Mu Hada horse camp, Yangxi border Suluk cattle and sheep herds, black cattle camp, and Yangxi border cattle camp.

sentences.zh: 凡馬牡曰兒，牝曰果，不及三歲曰駒，及壯擇割其牡曰騸。

translations.literal: For horses, males were called er, females guo, those under three years foals, and when mature selected stallions were gelded and called shan.
translations.idiomatic: Stallions were called er, mares guo, animals under three years foals; mature selected males were gelded as shan.

sentences.zh: 別其騍騸以為群，率騍馬五配兒馬一，群無過四百匹。

translations.literal: Mares and geldings were separated into herds; generally five mares were matched to one stallion, and no herd exceeded four hundred head.
translations.idiomatic: Mares and geldings formed separate herds at a ratio of five mares to one stallion, with no herd exceeding 400 head.

sentences.zh: 騍馬及羊三年一平群，牛六年，騍馬群三歲以息補耗，三馬而取一駒，騸馬群歲耗其十一。

translations.literal: Mare herds and sheep were balanced every three years, cattle every six; mare herds replenished losses with increase every three years, taking one foal per three mares; gelding herds annually lost one in eleven.
translations.idiomatic: Mare and sheep herds were rebalanced every three years, cattle every six; mare herds replaced losses at one foal per three mares, while gelding herds counted an annual loss of one in eleven.

sentences.zh: 置牧長、牧副、牧丁任其事，轄以協領、翼長、總管，官兵皆察哈爾、蒙古人充之。

translations.literal: Herdsmen chiefs, deputies, and hands were appointed to the task, supervised by assistant commandants, wing commanders, and superintendents; officers and soldiers were all filled by Chakhar and Mongol men.
translations.idiomatic: Herdsmen chiefs, deputies, and hands ran the herds under assistant commandants, wing commanders, and superintendents—all Chakhar and Mongol personnel.

sentences.zh: 飼秣所需木槽鏇钁鑹杓，每群各二，五年一給之。

translations.literal: Wooden troughs, augers, hoes, sickles, and ladles needed for feeding were two per herd, issued every five years.
translations.idiomatic: Each herd received two sets every five years of troughs, augers, hoes, sickles, and ladles for feeding.

sentences.zh: 總管三年番代。

translations.literal: Superintendents rotated every three years.
translations.idiomatic: Superintendents rotated on a three-year term.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，定牧群牲畜歲終彙報增減數目，視其贏絀，以第賞罰。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year it was fixed that at year's end herd livestock increases and decreases were compiled and reported; according to surplus or deficit, rewards and punishments were ranked.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 24 (1685) required year-end reports on herd increases and losses, with ranked rewards and punishments based on surplus or deficit.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，令八旗豢馬，春夏驅赴察哈爾牧放，曰出青，秋冬迴圈，曰回青。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Eight Banners' kept horses were ordered in spring and summer driven to Chakhar for pasturing, called going out to green; in autumn and winter they returned to the corrals, called returning to green.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 26 (1687) ordered banner horses driven to Chakhar for summer grazing (chuqing) and returned to corrals in autumn (huiqing).

sentences.zh: 四十四年，將軍楊福請市馬給兵丁，上不許，諭曰：「朝廷屢以太僕寺廠馬並茶馬給各兵丁，故無賠馬之苦。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year General Yang Fu requested purchasing horses to supply soldiers; the emperor did not permit it and instructed: "The court has repeatedly given Court of the Imperial Stud pasture horses and tea-horse trade horses to each soldier, so there is no hardship of compensating for horses.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 44 (1705) General Yang Fu asked to buy horses for the troops; the emperor refused, noting that stud and tea-horse allocations spared soldiers the burden of replacing mounts themselves.

sentences.zh: 歷觀宋、明議馬政，皆無善策。

translations.literal: Looking through Song and Ming discussions of horse policy, none had good measures.
translations.idiomatic: Song and Ming debates on horse policy had produced no lasting solution.

sentences.zh: 牧馬惟口外最善，水草肥美，不糜餉而孳生甚多。

translations.literal: Pasturing horses beyond the passes alone is best; water and grass are rich and fine, without consuming pay yet multiplying greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Pasture beyond the passes is best: rich grass and water multiply herds without draining the treasury.

sentences.zh: 如驅入內地牧之，即日費萬金不足矣。」

translations.literal: If driven into the interior to pasture, ten thousand in gold per day would not suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Drive them inland to graze and ten thousand taels a day would not cover the cost.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年，定在廠馬以四萬匹為率。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongzheng pasture horses were fixed at forty thousand as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzheng 3 (1725) set the pasture horse quota at 40,000.

sentences.zh: 至乾隆五年，足額外，溢七千餘匹。

translations.literal: By the fifth year of Qianlong, beyond filling the quota, there was a surplus of more than seven thousand.
translations.idiomatic: By Qianlong 5 (1740) the quota was met with 7,000 horses to spare.

sentences.zh: 兩翼牧廠，共騍馬百六十群，騸馬十六群，令分在兩翼廠牧放。

translations.literal: The two-wing pastures together had one hundred sixty mare herds and sixteen gelding herds, ordered distributed between the two-wing pastures for grazing.
translations.idiomatic: The two-wing pastures held 160 mare herds and 16 gelding herds, distributed between them for grazing.

sentences.zh: 八年，敕牧界毋許侵越。

translations.literal: In the eighth year an edict forbade encroachment on pasture boundaries.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong 8 (1743) forbade encroachment on pasture boundaries.

sentences.zh: 先是甘、涼、肅三州及西寧各設馬廠，分五群，群儲牝馬二百匹，牡四十。

translations.literal: Earlier Gansu, Liangzhou, and Suzhou prefectures and Xining each established horse pastures divided into five herds, each herd keeping two hundred mares and forty stallions.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Gansu, Liangzhou, Suzhou, and Xining each established pastures of five herds holding 200 mares and 40 stallions per herd.

sentences.zh: 尋改甘州廠屬巴里坤。

translations.literal: Soon the Ganzhou pasture was transferred to Barkul jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: The Ganzhou pasture was soon reassigned to Barkul.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，伊犁設孳生馬駝廠，畀錫伯、察哈爾、索倫、厄魯特四營牧之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year a breeding horse and camel pasture was established at Ili, assigned to the Xibe, Chakhar, Solon, and Oirat four camps for pasturing.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong 25 (1760) established an Ili breeding pasture for horses and camels, tended by Xibe, Chakhar, Solon, and Oirat camps.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，定牧廠官屬所需馬，視內地驛傳例，按官品給之，不得逾額。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year horses needed by pasture officials were fixed according to the interior courier-post precedent, given by official rank, and exceeding the quota was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong 32 (1767) set pasture officials' mounts by rank on the interior courier model, with no excess permitted.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶中，從都統慶溥言，撤回厄魯特人牧廠。

translations.literal: During Jiaqing, following banner commander Qing Pu's statement, the Oirat people's pasture was withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiaqing, at banner commander Qing Pu's urging, the Oirat pasture was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 初，富俊建言，撤大凌河牧廠，分歸東三省，仁宗嚴諭斥之。

translations.literal: Earlier Fu Jun memorialized to abolish the Daling River pasture and divide it among the three eastern provinces; the Jiaqing Emperor sternly rebuked this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Fu Jun had proposed abolishing the Daling River pasture and dividing it among the northeast provinces; the Jiaqing emperor rebuked him sharply.

sentences.zh: 迨道光七年，上經杏山東閱馬廠，見河岸馬群壯整。

translations.literal: By the seventh year of Daoguang the emperor passed east of Xingshan to inspect the horse pasture and saw herds along the riverbank sturdy and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Daoguang 7 (1827) the emperor inspected pastures east of Xingshan and saw sturdy, well-formed herds along the river.

sentences.zh: 因諭是間牧廠寬闊，水草蕃滋，馬恃以生息，若輕議裁，則散之甚易，聚之甚難。

translations.literal: He therefore instructed that these pastures were broad, water and grass abundant, and horses relied on them to multiply; if lightly discussed for cutting, dispersing would be very easy but gathering very difficult.
translations.idiomatic: He warned that these broad pastures with rich grass sustained the herds—cutting them would be easy to propose but ruinously hard to reverse.

sentences.zh: 再有率為此請者，以違制論。

translations.literal: Whoever again rashly made such a request would be judged for violating regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who rashly proposed such cuts again would be charged with violating regulations.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，科爾沁親王僧格林沁剿捻，檄取察哈爾戰馬六百匹，不堪乘用，奏聞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng Prince Senggelinqin of Horqin, suppressing the Nian rebels, requisitioned six hundred Chakhar war horses; they were unfit for riding, and this was reported.
translations.idiomatic: Xianfeng 4 (1854) Prince Senggelinqin of Horqin, fighting the Nian, requisitioned 600 Chakhar war horses—they proved unrideable, and he reported it.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，嚴諭都統慶昀整頓，蓋馬政漸衰弛矣。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and sternly ordered banner commander Qing Yun to rectify matters—for horse administration was gradually declining.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered banner commander Qing Yun to set things right—horse administration was clearly in decline.

sentences.zh: 光緒九年，太僕寺言兩翼騍馬騸馬一百十四群，並孳生馬五群，駝亦五群，較乾隆時群數大減。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Guangxu the Court of the Imperial Stud reported that the two wings had one hundred fourteen mare and gelding herds plus five breeding horse herds and five camel herds—far fewer herds than in the Qianlong era.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxu 9 (1883) the Court of the Imperial Stud reported only 114 mare and gelding herds plus five breeding horse and five camel herds—a sharp drop from Qianlong levels.

sentences.zh: 嗣是穆圖善練兵，至黑龍江求馬無良，愀然曰：「地氣其盡乎！」

translations.literal: Thereafter Mutushan trained troops; reaching Heilongjiang to seek horses he found none sound and said mournfully: "Has the land's vital force been exhausted?
translations.idiomatic: Later Mutushan, drilling troops in Heilongjiang, found no sound horses and mourned, "Has the land's vitality run out?

sentences.zh: 迨於末葉，厲行新法，舊時牧政益廢不講，豈非時勢使然歟？

translations.literal: By the dynasty's last years, vigorously implementing new methods, the old pasture administration was increasingly abandoned and neglected—is this not what the times compelled?
translations.idiomatic: In the dynasty's final years, zeal for reform left the old pasture system neglected—is that not simply how the times had turned?

sentences.zh: 順治初，陝西設洮岷、河州、西寧、庄浪、甘州茶馬司，及開成、安定、廣寧、黑水、清平、萬安、武安七監，歲遣御史一人專理之。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi Shaanxi established the Taomin, Hezhou, Xining, Zhuanglang, and Ganzhou tea-horse offices, plus seven supervisorates—Kaicheng, Anding, Guangning, Heishui, Qingping, Wan'an, and Wu'an—and each year one censor was dispatched exclusively to manage them.
translations.idiomatic: Early Shunzhi, Shaanxi established five tea-horse offices and seven supervisorates, with an annual censor dispatched to oversee them.

sentences.zh: 七年，喀爾喀、額魯特來市馬，諭令自章京監察之販客及賈人，與不系披甲者，概不許購，違者鞭一百，馬入官。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Khalkha and Oirat came to trade horses; an edict ordered that from the rank of zhangjing supervising traders and merchants, and those not wearing armor, none were permitted to purchase; violators received one hundred lashes and horses entered government custody.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi 7 (1650) Khalkha and Oirat horse traders were told that only armored soldiers under zhangjing supervision might buy—others faced 100 lashes and confiscation.

sentences.zh: 蒙古攜馬來京，不許商販私買，胥役私購者罪之。

translations.literal: When Mongols brought horses to the capital, merchants were not permitted private purchase; clerks and runners who bought privately were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Mongols bringing horses to the capital could not sell to private merchants; yamen runners who bought privately were punished.

sentences.zh: 康熙七年，裁茶馬御史，以馬政歸甘肅巡撫。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kangxi the tea-horse censor was abolished and horse administration returned to the Gansu governor.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 7 (1668) abolished the tea-horse censor and placed horse policy under the Gansu governor.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，諭遣師中等往蒙古諸旗購馬，歸化城、科爾沁各二千匹，餘定額有差。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year an edict dispatched Shi Zhong and others to purchase horses in the Mongol banners: two thousand each for Guihuacheng and Horqin, with fixed differing quotas for the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 34 (1695) sent Shi Zhong and others to buy horses in Mongol banners—2,000 each from Guihuacheng and Horqin, with graded quotas elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十二年，禁朝鮮買馬。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Qianlong Korea was forbidden to buy horses.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong 12 (1747) banned Korean horse purchases.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，敕烏魯木齊市易哈薩克馬百三十餘匹歸巴里坤。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year an edict ordered more than one hundred thirty Kazakh horses traded at Urumqi sent to Barkul.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong 25 (1760) ordered 130-odd Kazakh horses bought at Urumqi sent to Barkul.

sentences.zh: 旋以五吉等言，選哈薩克所易馬撥往巴里坤，遂停購買。

translations.literal: Soon, following Wuji and others' statement, Kazakh traded horses were selected and allocated to Barkul, and purchasing was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, on Wuji's advice, selected Kazakh trade horses went to Barkul and purchases ceased.

sentences.zh: 阿桂言伊犁易來哈薩克馬漸成大群，敕書嘉予。

translations.literal: Agui reported that Kazakh horses traded at Ili were gradually forming large herds; an edict praised and rewarded this.
translations.idiomatic: Agui reported that Kazakh horses traded at Ili were forming large herds; the throne praised and rewarded the achievement.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，定江寧、浙江、福建駐防馬匹出口採買例。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year regulations were fixed for Jiangning, Zhejiang, and Fujian garrisons' horses to be procured by export purchase.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong 28 (1763) set rules for Jiangning, Zhejiang, and Fujian garrisons to buy horses through export trade.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，以伊犁易哈薩克馬累積至多，擇巴里坤善地牧放。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, because Kazakh horses traded at Ili had accumulated greatly, good pasture at Barkul was selected for grazing.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong 32 (1767) sent accumulated Ili Kazakh trade horses to good Barkul pasture.

sentences.zh: 尋烏里雅蘇台馬缺，亦以哈薩克馬換易之。

translations.literal: Soon Uliastai had a horse shortage and also exchanged Kazakh horses to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: When Uliastai ran short, Kazakh horses filled the gap there too.

sentences.zh: 陝、甘營馬，例調自伊犁轉補，道遠耗時。

translations.literal: Shaanxi and Gansu garrison horses were routinely transferred for replenishment from Ili, the route distant and time-consuming.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi and Gansu garrisons routinely drew replacements from distant Ili—a slow, costly route.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，用賡福請，由伊犁、塔爾巴哈台隨地變價，令各營自購。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng, following Yong Fu's request, horses at Ili and Tarbagatai were sold locally at adjusted prices and each garrison ordered to purchase on its own.
translations.idiomatic: Xianfeng 4 (1854) Yong Fu's memorial let garrisons sell Ili and Tarbagatai stock locally and buy replacements themselves.

sentences.zh: 七年，並敕山東缺額馬，亦就近買補雲。

translations.literal: In the seventh year it was also ordered that Shandong's shortfall in allotted horses likewise be bought and replenished nearby.
translations.idiomatic: Xianfeng 7 (1857) extended the same local-purchase rule to Shandong's horse shortfall.

sentences.zh: 貢馬昉於國初，歸化城土默特二旗，每歲四時貢馬百匹。

translations.literal: Tribute horses began at the dynasty's founding; the two Tumed banners of Guihuacheng presented one hundred horses each of the four seasons every year.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute horses date to the dynasty's founding, when Guihuacheng's two Tumed banners gave 100 horses each season—400 yearly.

sentences.zh: 順治十三年，吐魯番貢三百二十四匹，嗣減令貢西馬四匹，蒙古馬十匹。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Shunzhi Turfan presented three hundred twenty-four; later this was reduced to four western horses and ten Mongol horses.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi 13 (1656) Turfan sent 324 horses; later its tribute was cut to four western and ten Mongol horses.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，以邊外蒙古貢馬，沿途抑買，諭嚴禁之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi, because frontier Mongol tribute horses were forcibly bought along the route, an edict strictly forbade this.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 8 (1669) forbade forced purchases of Mongol tribute horses along the route.

sentences.zh: 三十年，諭土謝圖、車臣俱留汗號，貢白駝一、白馬八如初，自餘毋以九白進。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year an edict ordered that Tushiyetu and Tsetsen both retain their khan titles and present one white camel and eight white horses as before, but otherwise not present the nine whites.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 30 (1691) let Tushiyetu and Tsetsen khans keep their titles and the traditional one white camel and eight white horses, but ended other "nine white" gifts.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，喀爾喀蒙古獻駝馬，多不可計，感聖祖破噶爾丹，得歸原牧地也。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year Khalkha Mongols presented camels and horses beyond counting, moved by the sage emperor's defeat of Galdan and their return to original pasturelands.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 35 (1696) Khalkha Mongols sent countless camels and horses in gratitude for defeating Galdan and restoring their pastures.

sentences.zh: 四川各土司例貢及折徵馬，各營少者一、二匹，最多十二匹。

translations.literal: Sichuan native chieftains' routine tribute and commuted horse levies ranged from one or two per garrison at minimum to twelve at most.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan chieftains' tribute and commuted horse levies ran from one or two per garrison to twelve at most.

sentences.zh: 甘肅唐古特七族西喇古兒例貢馬匹，各營最多者八十二匹，少者遞減至二、三匹。

translations.literal: Gansu's seven Tangut Xilar Gu'er tribes' routine horse tribute reached eighty-two per garrison at most, decreasing to two or three at minimum.
translations.idiomatic: Gansu's seven Tangut Xilar Gu'er tribes gave up to 82 horses per garrison, down to two or three.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，諭四川土司折價馬每匹納銀十二兩，通省營馬改從驛馬例，納銀八兩，永著為令。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong an edict ordered Sichuan chieftains' commuted horses at twelve taels of silver per horse; the whole province's garrison horses shifted to the courier-horse precedent at eight taels, permanently established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong 1 (1736) set Sichuan chieftain horse commutation at 12 taels per horse and provincial garrison horses at 8 taels on the courier model—permanent law.

sentences.zh: 三十年，哈薩克沁德穆爾等獻馬。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year Kazakh Qinde Mu'er and others presented horses.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong 30 (1765) Kazakh leader Qinde Mu'er and others presented horses.

sentences.zh: 敕其餘馬赴伊犁，毋於喀什噶爾諸地貿易。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the remaining horses sent to Ili and not traded in Kashgar and other places.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered surplus horses sent to Ili, not traded at Kashgar or elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 尋令沙拉伯爾游牧之哈薩克，與沙拉伯爾一體貢馬。

translations.literal: Soon Kazakhs nomading at Shalabuer were ordered to present tribute horses together with Shalabuer as one.
translations.idiomatic: Kazakhs pasturing at Shalabuer were soon required to tribute horses on the same terms as Shalabuer itself.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，停葉爾羌進馬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing Yarkand's horse presentations were stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaqing 1 (1796) ended Yarkand's horse tribute.

sentences.zh: 十六年，諭烏里雅蘇台將軍等貢馬及備用馬選取之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year an edict ordered the Uliastai general and others to select from tribute horses and reserve horses.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaqing 16 (1811) ordered the Uliastai general and others to select from tribute and reserve horses.

sentences.zh: 又諭伊犁進馬，材具佶閒，足供御用，令正備貢各五匹，有私帶者，以違制論。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered Ili's presented horses, their quality excellent and sufficient for imperial use, fixed at five each for principal and reserve tribute; private extra horses would be judged for violating regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict fixed Ili's excellent tribute horses at five principal and five reserve; private extras would be punished as violations.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，從那彥成奏，青海屬玉樹番族歲納貢馬，據丁口數，依二十壯丁貢馬一匹例，按數遞裁。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang, following Nayancheng's memorial, Qinghai's Yushu Tibetan tribes' annual tribute horses, based on household registers and the precedent of one horse per twenty able-bodied men, were progressively reduced by number.
translations.idiomatic: Daoguang 2 (1822) Nayancheng's memorial cut Qinghai Yushu Tibetan tribute by household count at one horse per twenty able-bodied men.

sentences.zh: 涼州屬番族歲仍納馬一匹。

translations.literal: Liangzhou's subordinate Tibetan tribes still presented one horse annually.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou Tibetan tribes still gave one horse a year.

sentences.zh: 初內外蒙部多貴戚，每征伐，爭先輸馬、駝，漢、唐以來所未有也。

translations.literal: Early on inner and outer Mongol banners had many nobles; at each campaign they vied to present horses and camels—unprecedented since Han and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, Mongol nobles across inner and outer banners vied to supply horses and camels for every campaign—something unseen since Han and Tang times.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，察哈爾親王、郡王、貝勒等，聞三籓叛，各獻馬匹佐軍。

translations.literal: Early in Kangxi, Chakhar princes, commandery princes, and beile, hearing of the Three Feudatories' rebellion, each presented horses to assist the army.
translations.idiomatic: Early Kangxi, hearing of the Three Feudatories' revolt, Chakhar princes and beile rushed horses to support the army.

sentences.zh: 道光九年，章佳胡圖克圖捐馬百匹，收其半。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Daoguang the Zhangjia Khutuktu donated one hundred horses; half were accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Daoguang 9 (1829) the Zhangjia Khutuktu donated 100 horses; the court accepted half.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，察哈爾蒙旗捐馬千九百七十匹。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the Chakhar Mongol banners donated one thousand nine hundred seventy horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of his reign, Chakhar Mongol banners donated 1,970 horses.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，哲布尊丹巴等捐馬千匹，喀爾喀土謝圖等二千匹，錫林果勒盟長等三千匹，帝以其多，卻之。

translations.literal: Early in Xianfeng Jebtsundamba and others donated one thousand horses, Khalkha Tushiyetu two thousand, Xilin Gol league chiefs three thousand; the emperor, because they were too many, declined them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianfeng, Jebtsundamba donated 1,000 horses, Khalkha Tushiyetu 2,000, and Xilin Gol league chiefs 3,000—the emperor declined them as excessive.

sentences.zh: 嗣聞已在途中，令擇善地牧以待用。

translations.literal: Later learning they were already on the road, he ordered good pasture chosen to hold them until use.
translations.idiomatic: Learning they were already en route, he ordered good pasture found to hold them until needed.

sentences.zh: 自是三音諾顏部等，以軍事輸馬、駝，旋捐馬二千一百，錫林果勒盟等千二百，或留或否。

translations.literal: From then the Setsen Khan departments and others, for military affairs, supplied horses and camels; soon two thousand one hundred horses were donated, Xilin Gol league one thousand two hundred—some kept, some declined.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Setsen Khan banners and others supplied horses and camels for the war effort; soon came donations of 2,100 horses and 1,200 from Xilin Gol—some accepted, some refused.

sentences.zh: 七年，各部落蒙古王等捐馬六千四百匹，詔納之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Mongol princes of various tribes donated six thousand four hundred horses; an edict accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Mongol princes of various tribes donated 6,400 horses, and an edict ordered them accepted.

sentences.zh: 時粵、捻擾畿東，利於用騎也。

translations.literal: At the time Guangdong and Nian rebels disturbed the capital region—advantageous for using cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Guangdong and Nian rebels were ravaging the capital region, and cavalry was urgently needed.

sentences.zh: 同治間，黑龍江將軍德英於呼倫貝爾各城勸捐軍馬。

translations.literal: During Tongzhi the Heilongjiang general De Ying urged donation of army horses in the cities of Hulun Buir.
translations.idiomatic: During Tongzhi, Heilongjiang general De Ying urged military horse donations across the Hulun Buir region.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，豐紳托克湍辦海防，時昭烏達盟郡王捐馬六百匹，因請踵行推廣勸諭，以助軍實雲。

translations.literal: Early in Guangxu Fengshen Tuoketuan handled coastal defense; at that time a Zhaowuda league commandery prince donated six hundred horses, and therefore requested extending encouragement broadly to aid military resources.
translations.idiomatic: Early Guangxu, while Fengshen Tuoketuan managed coastal defense, a Zhaowuda league prince donated 600 horses and asked that the encouragement be extended broadly to bolster the army.

sentences.zh: 驛置肇自前漢，歷代因之。

translations.literal: Courier stations began in Former Han; successive dynasties continued them.
translations.idiomatic: Courier stations date to the Former Han dynasty and were continued by every dynasty thereafter.

sentences.zh: 清沿明制，設驛馬，為額四萬三千三百有奇。

translations.literal: The Qing followed the Ming system and established courier horses, with a quota of forty-three thousand three hundred-odd.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing followed Ming practice and maintained courier horses at a quota of 43,300-odd.

sentences.zh: 各省驛制，定於康熙二年，凡齎奏官驛馬之數，各籓馬五匹，公、將軍、提督、督、撫三匹，總兵、巡鹽御史二匹，從兵部侍郎石麟請也。

translations.literal: Each province's courier system was fixed in the second year of Kangxi: for memorial-bearing officials' courier horses, feudatory princes five, dukes, generals, provincial commanders, governors, and governors-general three, regional commanders and salt-route censors two—following Vice Minister of War Shi Lin's request.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial courier regulations were set in Kangxi 2 (1663): feudatory princes received five relay horses, dukes and governors three, regional commanders and salt censors two—at the request of Vice Minister Shi Lin of the Board of War.

sentences.zh: 邊外之驛，定於九年，凡明詔特遣，及理籓院飭赴蒙古諸部宣諭公務，得乘邊外驛馬。

translations.literal: Frontier couriers were fixed in the ninth year: all imperially dispatched envoys and Lifan Yuan missions ordered to Mongol banners for proclamations could ride frontier courier horses.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier courier rules were set in Kangxi 9 (1670): imperial envoys and Lifan Yuan missions to Mongol banners could use frontier relay horses.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，征噶爾丹，設邊外五處驛站，用便車糧運輸。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, campaigning against Galdan, five frontier courier stations were established to facilitate grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 35 (1696), during the Galdan campaign, five frontier courier stations were set up to move grain and supplies.

sentences.zh: 又從理籓院言，自張家口外設蒙古驛。

translations.literal: Also following the Lifan Yuan's statement, Mongol couriers were established beyond Zhangjiakou.
translations.idiomatic: On the Lifan Yuan's recommendation, Mongol courier posts were also established beyond Zhangjiakou.

sentences.zh: 其大略也。

translations.literal: That was the general outline.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the general arrangement.

sentences.zh: 驛傳在僻地者，僅供本州縣所需，亦曰遞馬，額不過數匹。

translations.literal: Courier relays in remote places only supplied local prefecture and county needs, also called relay horses, with quotas of only a few.
translations.idiomatic: Remote courier posts served only local county needs—these relay horses numbered just a few per station.

sentences.zh: 沖繁州縣，置驛或二或三，額馬至六七十匹。

translations.literal: Busy prefectures and counties had two or three posts, with quotas reaching sixty or seventy horses.
translations.idiomatic: Busy counties maintained two or three posts with quotas of up to 60 or 70 horses.

sentences.zh: 驛差大者，皇華使臣，朝貢蕃客，餘如大臣入覲、蒞官、視鹺、監稅皆是。

translations.literal: Major courier missions included imperial envoys and tribute-bearing foreign guests; others such as grand ministers attending court, taking office, inspecting salt, and supervising tax collection were all the same.
translations.idiomatic: Major relay missions served imperial envoys and tribute missions, as well as ministers attending court, taking office, inspecting salt, or supervising tax collection.

sentences.zh: 若齎奏員役，呈奉表冊，其小者也。

translations.literal: Memorial-bearing clerks presenting documents were the minor sort.
translations.idiomatic: Minor missions included clerks carrying memorials and documents.

sentences.zh: 要者，如星馳飛遞，刻期立赴之屬。

translations.literal: Urgent ones were like star dispatch and flying relay, missions with fixed deadlines.
translations.idiomatic: Urgent cases included star dispatch and deadline missions requiring immediate delivery.

sentences.zh: 若閔勞恤死，允給郵傳，其散者也。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous ones were like condolence missions granted relay privileges.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous cases included condolence missions granted relay privileges.

sentences.zh: 驛政弊壞，張汧嘗極言之。

translations.literal: Courier administration's abuses Zhang Qian once spoke of forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qian once spoke forcefully about the corruption of courier administration.

sentences.zh: 越數誅求，橫索滋擾，蠹國病民，勢所必至。

translations.literal: Excessive demands across successive stations, arbitrary exactions and growing harassment—harming the state and afflicting the people—were inevitable.
translations.idiomatic: Excessive demands at every station and arbitrary exactions were inevitable—they drained the treasury and burdened the people.

sentences.zh: 已定例諸驛額馬，每年十踣其三，循例買補。

translations.literal: It was fixed by regulation that of each post's allotted horses, three in ten died yearly and were replaced by purchase per precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations fixed that three in ten allotted courier horses died each year and were replaced by purchase.

sentences.zh: 咸豐中，粵氛孔熾，湖、湘境為賊據，劫失驛騎，焚毀號舍，往往有之。

translations.literal: During Xianfeng the Guangdong crisis burned fiercely; Hunan and Hubei territory was held by rebels; courier horses were looted and station buildings burned—this often occurred.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianfeng, as the Taiping crisis raged and rebels held Hunan and Hubei, courier horses were looted and station buildings burned—often repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 各州縣或買馬填補，或賃馬應差，其有失驛未設，即雇夫代馬。

translations.literal: Each prefecture and county either bought horses to fill quotas or rented horses for missions; where posts were lost and not re-established, porters were hired in place of horses.
translations.idiomatic: Counties bought or rented horses to meet quotas; where posts had been destroyed, they hired porters instead.

sentences.zh: 甘肅舊設馬額六千餘，亦以軍興廢弛。

translations.literal: Gansu formerly had a horse quota of more than six thousand; it too fell into neglect because of warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Gansu's former quota of 6,000-odd horses also fell into neglect during the wars.

sentences.zh: 光緒九年，軍務既平，驛遞漸簡，所留馬視前減三分二，而驛政亦無所妨。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Guangxu, military affairs having settled, courier relay was gradually simplified; horses retained were reduced by two-thirds compared with before, yet courier administration was not impaired.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxu 9 (1883), with the wars over, courier service was simplified; horse quotas were cut by two-thirds without impairing operations.

sentences.zh: 十一年，新疆南路設驛。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year couriers were established on Xinjiang's southern route.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxu 11 (1885) established courier posts on Xinjiang's southern route.

sentences.zh: 是時，綜通國驛站歲費，約三百萬餘金。

translations.literal: At that time, totaling the empire's courier stations' annual expense, it was about three million-odd in cash.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the empire's courier system cost roughly three million taels a year.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，劉坤一、張之洞條陳新法，謂驛站耗財，不如仿外人之郵政。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Liu Kunyi and Zhang Zhidong memorialized on new methods, saying courier stations wasted funds and it would be better to imitate foreigners' postal service.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxu 29 (1903) Liu Kunyi and Zhang Zhidong proposed reforms, arguing that courier stations wasted money and that China should adopt Western-style postal service.

sentences.zh: 郵政遞信速，驛政文報遲。

translations.literal: Postal service delivered letters quickly; courier administration's documents were slow.
translations.idiomatic: Postal mail moved quickly; courier documents moved slowly.

sentences.zh: 弊由有驛州縣馬缺額，又復疲瘦，驛丁或倚為利藪，因致稽延。

translations.literal: The abuse arose because counties with posts had horses below quota, again thin and weak; courier runners sometimes treated this as a profit source, thus causing delays.
translations.idiomatic: The problem was understaffed, emaciated horses and couriers who treated shortages as a source of profit, causing endless delays.

sentences.zh: 請設驛政局，推行郵政，俾驛鋪經費專取給郵資，即三百萬歲耗可以省出矣。

translations.literal: They requested establishing a courier administration bureau, promoting postal service, so that station expenses would be funded solely from postage—then the three million yearly waste could be saved.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed a courier bureau and postal service funded by postage alone, saving the three million taels spent annually.

sentences.zh: 時韙其言。

translations.literal: At the time their words were approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved at the time.

sentences.zh: 已而驛馬漸裁，嗣是驛遂廢不用。

translations.literal: Soon courier horses were gradually cut; thereafter couriers were abandoned and unused.
translations.idiomatic: Courier horses were gradually cut back, and the old relay system was eventually abandoned.

sentences.zh: 順治初，建常盈庫，凡車駕司朋椿站銀，武庫司馬值，太僕寺馬價皆儲之。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi the Ever-Full Treasury was established; all the Carriage Office's companion and relay silver, the Arsenal's horse prices, and the Court of the Imperial Stud's horse prices were stored there.
translations.idiomatic: Early Shunzhi established the Ever-Full Treasury to hold funds for the Carriage Office, the Arsenal's horse accounts, and the Court of the Imperial Stud's horse prices.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，改常盈庫儲歸戶部。

translations.literal: Early in Kangxi the Ever-Full Treasury's reserves were transferred to the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Early Kangxi transferred the Ever-Full Treasury to the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十六年，敕雲南營馬除十踣其三按例應賠外，其逾額踣斃者免賠椿銀。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Qianlong an edict ordered that for Yunnan garrison horses, beyond the three in ten deaths requiring compensation per regulation, excess deaths were exempt from peichun silver.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong 16 (1751) exempted Yunnan garrison troops from compensation silver for horse deaths beyond the regulated three-in-ten annual loss.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，定給留圈馬乾，每匹視綠營稍優異。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year fodder allowances for corral-kept horses were fixed, each horse slightly more generous than for the Green Standard Army.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong 27 (1762) set fodder allowances for corral horses slightly above Green Standard rates.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，又令雲南買補馬價，每匹減銀三兩。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year Yunnan's horse replacement purchase price was again ordered reduced by three taels of silver per horse.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong 38 (1773) cut Yunnan's horse replacement price by three taels per head.

sentences.zh: 初馬乾歲費約四十四萬有奇。

translations.literal: Initially annual fodder expense was about four hundred forty thousand-odd.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, annual fodder costs ran to roughly 440,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 道光中，從載銓等言，裁八旗官拴馬半額，以節出之費補兵餉焉。

translations.literal: During Daoguang, following Zai Quan and others' statement, banner officers' tethered-horse allowances were cut by half, using the savings to supplement troop pay.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daoguang, at Zai Quan's urging, banner officers' horse allowances were halved and the savings applied to troop pay.

sentences.zh: 清初定現任官得養馬，餘悉禁之。

translations.literal: Early Qing fixed that only incumbent officials might keep horses; all others were forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Early Qing law allowed only incumbent officials to keep horses; everyone else was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 尋許武進士、武舉、兵丁、捕役養馬。

translations.literal: Soon military licentiates, military graduates, soldiers, and constables were permitted to keep horses.
translations.idiomatic: Soon military degree-holders, soldiers, and constables were also permitted horses.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，禁民人養馬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi common people were forbidden to keep horses.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 1 (1662) forbade commoners to keep horses.

sentences.zh: 有私販馬匹，為人首告者，馬給首告之人。

translations.literal: If private horse trading was reported by an informer, the horse was given to the informer.
translations.idiomatic: Private horse traders reported by informers forfeited their horses to the accuser.

sentences.zh: 其主有官職，予重罰。

translations.literal: If the owner held office, heavy punishment was imposed.
translations.idiomatic: Official owners received heavy punishment.

sentences.zh: 平民荷校鞭責。

translations.literal: Commoners received cangue and lashes.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners wore the cangue and were flogged.

sentences.zh: 十年，令民人仍得養馬。

translations.literal: In the tenth year common people were again permitted to keep horses.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 10 (1671) again permitted commoners to keep horses.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，定出廠馬、駝，或踐食田禾，或縱逸侵擾，兵鞭責，官罰俸有差。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year it was fixed that pasture horses and camels leaving the grounds, whether trampling crops or straying to harass, brought lashes for soldiers and graded salary fines for officials.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 26 (1687) fixed that pasture animals damaging crops or straying brought lashes for soldiers and graded fines for officials.

sentences.zh: 其兵丁強人代牧，乃勒索擾累者，兵發刑部，官降調。

translations.literal: If soldiers forced others to herd for them and extorted and harassed, soldiers were sent to the Ministry of Justice and officials demoted or transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers who forced others to herd for them and extorted payment were sent to the Ministry of Justice; their officers were demoted.

sentences.zh: 凡牧馬斃，則驗其皮，踣斃例須賠抵，有一九、一七之罰。

translations.literal: Whenever herd horses died, the hide was inspected; death in service required compensation, with penalties of nineteen-twentieths or seventeen-twentieths.
translations.idiomatic: When a herd horse died, its hide was inspected; death in service required compensation at nineteen-twentieths or seventeen-twentieths of value.

sentences.zh: 應取駒千匹者，以百匹為一分，百匹者以十匹為一分。

translations.literal: Where one thousand foals were due, one hundred formed a unit; where one hundred, ten formed a unit.
translations.idiomatic: Where 1,000 foals were due, they were counted in units of 100; where 100, in units of 10.

sentences.zh: 雍正十三年，定馬、駝出廠時，毛齒皆有冊，回日覈驗，如疲瘠十不及三，免議，否則兵鞭責，官罰俸有差。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng it was fixed that when horses and camels left pasture, coat and teeth were all registered; on return they were verified—if fewer than three in ten were emaciated, no inquiry; otherwise soldiers were lashed and officials fined by grade.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzheng 13 (1735) required coat and teeth registered when animals left pasture; on return, if fewer than three in ten were emaciated there was no penalty—otherwise soldiers were lashed and officials fined.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，禁牧丁等盜馬私售，及與人乘，峻其科罰。

translations.literal: Early in Qianlong herdsmen and others were forbidden to steal horses for private sale or let others ride them; penalties were severe.
translations.idiomatic: Early Qianlong forbade herdsmen from stealing pasture horses for private sale or lending them for riding, with severe penalties.

sentences.zh: 十六年，嚴牧馬減克料草之罪。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year penalties were tightened for herd horses' withheld fodder.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong 16 (1751) tightened penalties for withholding herd horses' fodder.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，官馬出青，每百匹准倒十匹，逾額勒其買補。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, when government horses went out to summer pasture, ten deaths per hundred were permitted; beyond the quota they were compelled to buy replacements.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong 28 (1763) allowed ten deaths per hundred government horses sent to summer pasture; excess deaths required purchase of replacements.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十一年，行圍木蘭，查獲私販馬匹諸犯，重懲之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jiaqing, during the Mulan hunting encampment, private horse traders and other offenders were discovered and heavily punished.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaqing 11 (1806), during the Mulan hunt, private horse traders were caught and heavily punished.

sentences.zh: 因諭：「我朝講武時巡，扈從均給官馬。

translations.literal: He therefore instructed: "Our dynasty emphasizes martial training and seasonal tours; the entourage all receive government horses.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore decreed: "Our dynasty emphasizes martial training and seasonal tours, and the entire entourage receives government horses.

sentences.zh: 大臣祿入較優，給馬較少。

translations.literal: Ministers' salaries are comparatively generous, so fewer horses are allotted.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers receive generous salaries and therefore fewer horses.

sentences.zh: 官員兵丁，視差務之繁簡，定馬數之多寡，少者一、二匹，多至五匹，事竣原馬還官。

translations.literal: Officials and soldiers, according to the complexity of their duties, were allotted more or fewer horses—from one or two at minimum to five at most; when the task ended the original horses were returned to government.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and soldiers received one to five horses depending on duty complexity, and returned them when the mission ended.

sentences.zh: 如踣斃，呈驗耳尾，仍按價折交。

translations.literal: If a horse died in service, ears and tail were presented for inspection and compensation was still paid at appraised price.
translations.idiomatic: If a horse died, ears and tail were presented for inspection and compensation paid at appraised value.

sentences.zh: 收放時，命王大臣督察。

translations.literal: When pasturing, princes and grand ministers were ordered to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and grand ministers were appointed to supervise pasturing.

sentences.zh: 乃官兵等竟私鬻官單，察哈爾官兵收馬利，其折銀易於買補。

translations.literal: Yet officers and soldiers actually sold official permits privately; Chakhar officers and soldiers profited from receiving horses, as cash compensation was easier than buying replacements.
translations.idiomatic: Yet officers and soldiers sold official permits privately; Chakhar troops preferred cash compensation because it was easier than replacing the horses.

sentences.zh: 積弊日深，大妨馬政。

translations.literal: Accumulated abuses grew daily deeper, greatly obstructing horse administration.
translations.idiomatic: Abuses deepened daily and gravely undermined horse administration.

sentences.zh: 自後設有賣單及折收者，一體科罰。

translations.literal: Henceforth whoever sold permits or accepted cash bribes would be punished alike.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth anyone selling permits or accepting cash compensation would be punished.

sentences.zh: 私買之馬販，從嚴問擬。

translations.literal: Private horse buyers would be sentenced strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Private horse buyers would be sentenced severely.

sentences.zh: 大臣等其妥議定章以聞。」

translations.literal: Ministers and others should properly deliberate and fix regulations to report.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers were to deliberate and submit regulations.

sentences.zh: 凡營馬或走脫竊失，責令賠補，謂之賠椿，年遞減十之一，至十年悉免之。

translations.literal: Whenever garrison horses escaped or were stolen, compensation was required, called peichun; it decreased by one-tenth yearly until after ten years all was exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison horses that escaped or were stolen had to be replaced under peichun compensation, reduced by one-tenth each year until fully exempt after ten years.

sentences.zh: 應敵傷損者免賠。

translations.literal: Those wounded in battle were exempt from compensation.
translations.idiomatic: Battle wounds exempted horses from compensation.

sentences.zh: 騎至三年踣斃者亦免。

translations.literal: Those ridden to three years and then dying in service were also exempt.
translations.idiomatic: Horses ridden for three years and then dying in service were also exempt.

sentences.zh: 其餘一年或二三年內踣斃，賠額視其省而異，以十金為最多。

translations.literal: For the rest, dying in service within one or two or three years, compensation amounts differed by province, with ten taels of gold as the maximum.
translations.idiomatic: Deaths within one to three years required compensation varying by province, up to a maximum of ten taels.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，定古北口盤獲私馬逾三十匹者送京，不及三十匹賞與兵丁，著為令。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi it was fixed that private horses seized at Gubeikou exceeding thirty head were sent to the capital; fewer than thirty were rewarded to soldiers—established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhi 2 (1863) fixed that private horses seized at Gubeikou in lots over 30 were sent to the capital; smaller lots were rewarded to soldiers—permanent law.
